_: The sentences index.html, careers.html and contact.html build after they have loaded.
es/strings.json holds the markup; this holds what the two step forms write
at runtime, because tools/build-es.mjs walks text nodes and never steps
inside a script block — a literal there may be a selector, a class name, or
a track name the database reads in English.
The key is the English sentence exactly as the page passes it to say().
Values arrive as {named} placeholders: every one that appears in a key must
appear in its translation too, or the sentence loses a number. Word order is
free, which is the whole reason they are named rather than concatenated.
TWO REGISTERS, on purpose, following es/strings.json rather than deciding
anything new. The careers dialog speaks to an applicant and uses tú ('¿A qué
áreas estás postulando?'); the seat form on the home page speaks to an
employer and uses usted ('El hueco que quiere cubrir, en su hora local.').
The seven sentences BOTH forms use are worded so they belong to neither —
no imperative, no possessive — because one entry cannot be both.
'most' and 'least' are looked up by say(freed) rather than written as a
literal, so the extractor in lib-seg.mjs cannot see them. They are needed
all the same and check.mjs knows not to call them stale. They read longer
here than the column headings of the same name in es/strings.json because
these go inside a sentence and those are labels over a column.
